items.title: Herb Morand Interview, 1950-03-12
items.q: I worked there a year and a half with little Joe Lindsey and his band.

ctx.x: I understand there was a dinner given in your honor and other jazz musicians in Chicago in 1935. Is that so?

Yeah, that was when I was at Tornis. I worked there a year and a half with little Joe Lindsey and his band. And Tornis was the headquarters for all greats like Lewis, Cab Calloway, Duke Ellington. And I have pictures of all that. Well, whenever they'd be in town, Tornis would invite them down. And Joe Lindsey used to be Lewis Armstrong's right-hand man, as they call it. And Lewis, all those greats would come there. And I used to play for them. And they'd sit down and enjoy. I have pictures on all that. And the…
All right. At that time, too, columnists began to refer to you as Louis Armstrong's stepson, more or less. Yeah, yeah.
